events.title: Demo updated: the first night is easier to survive
events.summary: The demo for Rules of the Inn (Nights 1–3) is updated. Steam Next Fest is on (it opened October 19 at 10:00 AM PDT). During it, I made the first night easier to get into. The first time you play, when the lamp first fades, the flame holds on until you pour oil. The first time you play, a prompt tells you to lower your eyes when the first shadow closes in. On the first launch after this update, a screen appears once to set the brightness. You can change it later in Options. Fixed gamepad controls

events.title: The rules on the wall may not be right tonight — Steam Next Fest demo (Oct 19–26)
events.summary: Rules of the Inn is taking part in Steam Next Fest, October 19-26, with a playable demo. Seven nights in one tatami room. Only the rules keep you alive. The rules are posted on the wall, but they may not be right tonight. Follow what you remember, get through the dark one night at a time, and see whether you can reach morning. events.title: The rules on the wall do not stay the same
events.summary: Up to seven rules are posted on the wall of this inn. Follow them and you will see the morning — that was the idea. But the rules change from night to night. The ink wears away. An unreadable line sinks, leaving only its number. Nails tear it open. What stood inside the torn band is anyone's guess. It is rewritten in vermilion, upside down. events.title: Guess Right, and the Inn Reveals One Thing
events.summary: During each night at the inn, you read the scrawls on the walls and the scraped-out names in the ledger, then fill the Book of Truth one line at a time. When your reading is correct, the inn reveals exactly one thing. No long explanation. One line, admitting that you were right. When it is wrong, the opposite happens. The inn rearranges itself to fit what you wrote. Your mistake is not corrected. Your mistake becomes the truth. We are polishing that moment of being right ahead of the November 5

events.title: The Book of Truth now reads like paper under a single lantern
events.summary: Before dawn, you sit down with the Book of Truth. What you saw and heard in the inn becomes a card, and the cards go into the blanks. Nothing haunts you here. The only thing that turns up is the fact of what you failed to notice. We reworked this page. The fibre and the laid lines of the washi are unchanged; only the rules, the shadows and the edges are cooled a little. events.title: The exceptions to the rules are re-drawn every run
events.summary: This inn has seven nights' worth of rules, one revealed each night. Those rules have exceptions: among the hauntings, some kill the ones who obey. Until now, which haunting was an exception never changed. Learn it once, and every later run was easy. The whole feeling of "the rules can betray you" was spent in a single playthrough. events.title: The trailer is up
events.summary: The trailer for Rules of the Inn is now available. It shows only what matters most in this inn: the lantern's flame, the rules that keep appearing on the wall, and the thing standing behind the paper screen. One rule is added every night, and a new rule never cancels an old one. So the further you go, the more you must hold in your head at once. That moment in the second half where the screen goes still and quiet — that is one of the rules. Out November 5, 2026. We'll also be at Steam Next Fest.

events.title: The Book of Truth was left beside my pillow
events.summary: Near daybreak, a book you have never seen is lying beside your pillow. On the cover, in ink, only this: The Book of Truth. A guest before you added a line in their own hand. — Write down what this inn truly is. Only those who finish may cross into morning. In this inn the rules multiply night after night. The ink on the wall wears thin, and some mornings a rule you were sure you had memorized can no longer be read. Before morning comes, you write into this book. Why every hand in the guestbook s

events.title: Do not lower your eyes for a small, pale hand
events.summary: The inn has seven rules, and some of them have exceptions. Rule III says: if you are touched, lower your eyes. But if the hand that touched you was small and pale, you must not. That is the hand of a child waiting to be met, and looking away means leaving them behind. The rules are written on the wall — but as the nights go on, the ink fades until you can no longer read them. Memorise them while you still can, or face the night without them. events.title: The Book of Truth — write down what you worked out before you leave
events.summary: Surviving the inn is only half of Rules of the Inn. Across seven nights, things happen here that nothing explains: the handwriting in the guest book, the paper on the wall that keeps being replaced, the shadows the lantern throws. All of it follows the inn's own reasoning. Before you leave, you sit down with the Book of Truth. The sentences on it have blanks, and you fill them with the words you remember from the nights. events.title: How long do the rules on the wall stay true?
events.summary: I. Keep the light burning. Seven rules hang on the wall. They are the house rules of this inn. Obey them, and dawn comes. These past days we have been rebuilding the room the rules live in. Tatami relaid in the Edo-style eight-mat auspicious layout, where no four corners meet at a single point, as in a real Japanese room The rush weave and the seams between mats now read on screen The room is lit again by two lights: the lantern flame and the moonlight through the shoji As the night deepens the

events.title: Building the dawn puzzle: the Book of Truth
events.summary: At every dawn, you face the Book of Truth Using only what you saw last night, you place words into the gaps. No one tells you whether you are right. All you get back is a feeling. The art has been repainted Lamplight, the grain of the paper, ink bleeding into it. The darkness of the inn itself has been rebuilt. events.title: You can now see how long you still have to endure
events.summary: When you shut your eyes and endure, the only thing telling you it was over was a sound. If you played with the sound off, it was a pitch-black screen and a guess. The length changes every time, so without a cue there was nothing to read. Added an arc in front of the eyelids that fills as you endure It appears only while you are enduring, and vanishes when you open your eyes You can now tell how much is left with the sound muted.

events.title: There is writing on the wall, left by the guests before you
events.summary: The rules are not the only thing posted on that wall. A new element in development: writing left behind by previous guests. Someone who tried to survive a night in this room before you, setting down in thin ink how they read the rules and where they were wrong. It is only legible while the lantern burns bright, which means the decision to pour oil or quell the flame as the rules demand now has one more thing riding on it. I got the placement wrong first. events.title: How the lantern was made
events.summary: The first rule of the inn is: "Never let the light die." Because that rule exists, the lantern's flame had to read as real fire. Is it about to go out, or will it hold? If the player can't answer that from the flicker alone, then the act of following the rule falls apart. At first I drove the brightness with random noise. That was a mistake. events.title: The demo is out now
events.summary: The Rules of the Inn demo is available now. The rules are posted on the wall of the inn. Keep them and morning comes. Break them and it does not. Nothing is hidden. The rules are written plainly, from the start. And still, you cannot be certain whether what you just saw was one of them. When a shadow falls on the paper screen — is it the inn's own shadow, or the one the rules warn about? That is yours to judge.
